questions.title: What a Constructor Is
questions.description: A constructor in Java is best described as:
questions.Option1: An ordinary method that must be called manually after the object exists
questions.Option2: A special member that shares the class name and runs automatically when an object is created with new
questions.Option3: A keyword that releases the memory of a destroyed object
questions.Option4: A static block that runs when the class is loaded

questions.description: Under which condition does the Java compiler supply a default (no-argument) constructor?
questions.Option2: Only when the class declares no constructor at all
questions.Option3: Only when the class has a parameterized constructor

questions.title: Parameterized Constructor Purpose
questions.description: A parameterized constructor is mainly used to:
questions.Option1: Initialize each new object with values supplied at creation time
questions.Option2: Create an exact duplicate of an existing object
questions.Option4: Give default values that can never be changed

questions.title: Overloading Difference Rule
questions.description: Two constructors of the same class are considered overloaded when they differ in:
questions.Option2: The spelling of the class name
questions.Option3: The number, types or order of their parameters

questions.title: Copy Constructor Availability
questions.description: Which statement about copy constructors in Java is TRUE?
questions.Option1: Java has no built-in copy constructor; programmers write one that takes an object of the same class as its argument
questions.Option2: Java automatically generates a copy constructor for every class
questions.Option3: A copy constructor must be declared static
questions.Option4: Object.clone() serves as the copy constructor of every class
